description:
From the 2026-08-19 gap audit of #152 vs ../foundationdb. Two holes, benign on the current branch only because shard/log families change solely in recovery's system transaction (whose content equals the unlock snapshot); both become real when the Distributor (q67.21) mutates shard_keys/ or layout mid-epoch:

1. Staleness race: finalize task N applies the window to RoutingData during resolution but sends {:routing_data_update} only after log push. A batch spawned in between snapshots metadata.version >= N (so the resolver will not re-send version N's entries) with a pre-N routing_data struct. The ETS shard table is immune (shared, mutated in place); log_map/log_services are per-struct - a layout_log change at version N is invisible to batch N+1's routing for the duration of batch N's log push. FDB prevents this with version-ordered stateMutations relay + shardChanged signaling (Resolver.actor.cpp:79-97).

2. No idempotence guard: Metadata.apply_updates is version-guarded; RoutingData.apply_mutations is not, and insert_log is non-idempotent (re-applied layout_log set appends a duplicate index). Overlapping windows to concurrent tasks are a documented protocol feature.

Fix shape: guarantee batch K+1 routes with all metadata <= K applied, and make RoutingData application version-guarded (e.g. fold log_map/log_services into the version-guarded server-side path, or route strictly from the in-task differential). Must land with or before q67.21's mid-epoch writer.

comments.text: PR #155 (stack #156, on #154) closes hole 1 (server folds version-filtered window entries into Metadata AND RoutingData in one step; ack+routing snapshot consistent by construction; {:routing_data_update} replacement retired) and hole 2 for both re-delivered windows (global version filter) and legitimate re-sets (insert_log now idempotent by log id). Cold audit interleaving analysis: invariant holds by induction, no counterexample on server struct state. RESIDUAL (audit finding 2, fixing as next stacked PR): the shared ETS shard table has multiple unordered writers - finalization tasks, now the server, and ShardRouter.get_logs_for_key's lazy in-row log-index cache. Counterexample: task A (window (v0,v1], K->tag1) sends its window to the server, is descheduled before its ETS write; server applies A then B ((v0,v2], K->tag2); A resumes and writes K->tag1 - permanent stale tag, never repaired (resolver acked past v1). Fix: versioned LWW shard rows {end_key, tag, version} written via atomic insert_new/select_replace, tombstoned clears, router skips tombstones, and the lazy cache is deleted (golden-ratio indices are cheap; the cache is an unversioned writer inside the read path). Also documenting audit finding 4: sharded-mode settle-lag (batch at cV can route before committed metadata at vN<cV from a prior batch settles across all resolvers) is an accepted trade-off vs FDB's single-pipeline guarantee; revisit under q67.22.

Residual closed by PR #157 (stack #156): shard rows are {end_key, tag, version} written via atomic insert_new/select_replace LWW; clears tombstone (:deleted) so late old sets cannot resurrect boundaries; router navigation skips tombstones; equal versions overwrite (in-transaction clear-then-set order preserved; identical replayed sequences converge); snapshot rows version nil lose to any commit. Lazy log-index cache and lookup_shards_for_range deleted (production-dead; the cache was an unversioned writer inside the read path). Cold audit: prior counterexample converges, no reachable new counterexamples (equal-version divergence impossible - confirms list canonical per version; fresh-key races serialize through ETS; clear_range boundary math exact). Noted for the future: (1) tombstones accumulate until recovery rebuilds the table - if shard churn becomes sustained, compact at recovery; (2) all-tombstones is transiently reachable between a rewrite's clear and sets under a concurrent routing task and raises 'No live shard boundaries' - crash lands in the batch task, acceptable pre-q67.21, revisit with the Distributor; (3) sharded settle-lag (audit finding 4 of PR #155) accepted vs FDB's single-pipeline guarantee, revisit under q67.22. Both q67.24 holes plus the ETS ordering residual are now closed - ticket complete pending stack review/merge.

Direction change per user + FDB study: PR #157 (versioned LWW rows + tombstones) withdrawn - it tolerated write disorder that FDB simply forbids. Replaced by PR #159 (stack #161): FDB postResolution shape - server applies each batch's committed metadata (window + own deferred) serialized in a PROXY-LOCAL batch sequence (latestLocalCommitBatchLogging analogue; NOT global sequencer versions, which interleave across proxies - cold audit caught that as a latent multi-proxy deadlock, fixed + pinned by test), then hands the task an IMMUTABLE routing snapshot (gb_trees replaces ETS entirely). Task splits+pushes in parallel outside the gate (sound because snapshots are immutable and Shale reorders pushes by version chain - stronger parallelism than FDB, same visible ordering). Apply-then-use gives same-batch visibility: the epoch's first restructuring commit routes itself. Net -400 lines: shared :public ETS + lifecycle, in-task window application, metadata side-messages/callbacks, lazy router cache all deleted. Audit verdicts: chain protocol correct (no deadlock in any single-proxy failure interleaving; ack-vs-snapshot consistent; sharded deferred semantics preserved); gb_trees ceiling search correct; FDB correspondence confirmed with citations. Bonus for q67.23: the ETS-reference crash class is now structurally impossible, and the unlock snapshot is just plain data. Closing again pending stack review.

title: RoutingData window application: version-guard and ordering for mid-epoch shard-map churn
